scientific_question: Can the frozen sequence model preserve within-batch target ordering when the same common human-plasma nanoparticle-corona aliquot is processed by previously unseen proteomics core facilities?

data_semantics.biological_unit_semantics: one pooled/common human plasma aliquot distributed to core facilities; technical rather than independent biological replication

source_processing.rank_scope: all positive numeric protein rows within each core facility, before frozen-target filtering
source_processing.missingness: retain a target row when at least one author replicate is numeric; average only available numeric replicates; exclude rows with no numeric replicate
source_processing.multi_accession_policy: retain only a single unambiguous frozen-target accession per source row; fail closed if a row maps to multiple frozen targets

outer_split.training_rule: all core facilities except one held-out core
outer_split.testing_rule: all eligible frozen-target observations from the held-out core

claim_boundary: This is a pre-registered exploratory technical cross-core portability analysis of a common pooled aliquot. It is not independent biological validation, cross-study validation, or evidence of generalization across donors or disease cohorts.
